message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, but left a few things and a note saying he didn't want to bring those things with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of their stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I saw him at a party, and we were being polite. He asked how the move-out went, and I said it was good. Then he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing I did wrong. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Okay, so to figure this out, I need to think about the different aspects of the situation. First, there's the legal aspect. I know that legally, I didn't do anything wrong because the landlord can dispose of the stuff if the tenant doesn't pick it up, and I followed that process. But that doesn't necessarily mean I did the morally right thing. Then there's the relationship aspect. He's upset with me, and that's affecting our relationship. Even though legally I'm in the right, making him upset might not be the best outcome. There's also the aspect of communication. I tried to contact him for two weeks, but he didn't respond. So, I took the initiative to get rid of his stuff to avoid the rip-off of the landlord charging us. But maybe I should have done something else, like stored his games somewhere or given him another chance to pick them up. Another thing to consider is the value of the games. He had 60 PS4 games, and I sold them for $600. That's a significant amount of money. Maybe I should have given him the money instead of keeping it for myself. But legally, since he abandoned the stuff, I might have a claim to it. Also, there's the aspect of intent. I didn't sell his games to be malicious; I did it to avoid the rip-off of the landlord charging us. But maybe I should have considered his feelings more and tried to handle it differently. I'm also thinking about what would have been the best course of action. Maybe I could have stored his games somewhere and given him another chance to pick them up, even after the two weeks. Or perhaps I could have reached out to him again through a different method, like a phone call, to make sure he knew about the situation. Another angle is the concept of ownership. Once he left the stuff, did it become my responsibility, or did he still retain ownership? Legally, it seems like he still owned the games, but by not responding, he might have forfeited some rights. I'm also wondering about the precedent this sets. If I take someone's stuff and sell it without their consent, even if it's to avoid a rip-off, does that set a bad precedent for how I handle similar situations in the future? Additionally, there's the aspect of empathy. How would I feel if someone sold my stuff without my consent, even if it was to avoid a rip-off? I might feel violated or upset, which is how he's feeling now. So, putting it all together, while I didn't do anything legally wrong, there might be some moral gray areas. I did what I thought was necessary to avoid financial loss, but it came at the cost of damaging our relationship and making him upset. Maybe the right thing to do would have been to find a balance between protecting my financial interests and respecting his ownership of the games. Perhaps I could have stored the games and given him another chance to pick them up, or even offered to give him the money from the sale if he wanted it. In the end, it's a tough situation because I was trying to do what I thought was right, but it ended up causing harm to our relationship. It makes me think that sometimes, doing what's legally right isn't always the same as doing what's morally right, and it's important to consider both aspects when making decisions.
